gate_design.kill_condition_verbatim: A04 is killed if ANY of the following three clauses fires. K1 -- no rule disagreement: across the arms, at every checkpoint on the pre-frozen grid where the PPL-plateau rule PLATEAU(T) accepts, the non-inferiority rule NI(delta) also accepts on at least 3 of the 4 capability axes; AND the count of (arm, checkpoint) cells where the two rules disagree is <= 1 out of >= 24 evaluated cells. K2 -- disagreement drowned by seed variance: for the primary axis (TriviaQA EM), the between-seed standard deviation of the calibrated residual at the pre-frozen apex checkpoint, pooled across arms with S >= 3 seeds each, is >= 50% of the smallest between-arm residual difference the paper wants to claim; equivalently, the one-sided 95% run-level bound t_{0.05,S-1} * sd_run / sqrt(S) exceeds the pre-registered non-inferiority margin delta = 10% of the intact arm's own calibrated residual on >= 2 of the 4 axes. K3 -- axes at floor: at the target scale, >= 3 of the 4 capability axes have the INTACT arm's calibrated residual (reported minus construct-appropriate best-constant null) below 5pp, or have every damaged arm indistinguishable from its own best-constant predictor at BH q=.05.

gate_design.primary_statistic: PER-ARM ONE-SIDED NON-INFERIORITY BOUND, deliberately NOT a rank correlation over rungs. B04 hit the n=6 exact-permutation floor (2/720=0.002778) TWICE on OLMo-2-7B and still died on Qwen3-8B (rho fell to +0.4286 p=0.42 / -0.4857 p=0.36, p x130-150) -- so maximal significance at n=6 is not evidence of a real effect, and adding rungs to buy permutation p is the move that failed. Power here comes from S (seeds) and item count n.

power_analysis.no_post_hoc_seed_addition: if the measured sd_run implies a bound > delta on >=2 axes, K2 FIRES rather than seeds being added post hoc. Adding seeds after seeing the variance is the selective-reporting move A01's gate-4 exists to prevent.
power_analysis.multiplicity: 4 axes x 4 arms x 6 checkpoints = 96 cells -> BH q=.05 across the whole declared family, family size declared in advance. One-sided NI bounds must not be silently mixed into a two-sided BH family.

same-arch/same-harness re-runs in this repo are BYTE-IDENTICAL (0 flips). Do not budget for or excuse anything as 'runtime noise' without a same-code control proving it.
